cultural.vision_reason: A wooden fish club with a carved human face head in Northwest Coast style, an object type used by Kwakwaka'wakw and neighboring peoples for dispatching fish; the record only describes it as "southern Northwest Coast style" without independent attribution evidence, but this is a widely-shared regional tool form consistent with the claimed group.

physical.title: club; fishing equipment
physical.summary: Short club of yew, used for fish, with large drop shaped head, and raised finial to the end of the shaft, of circular cross section, and a flat end. The head of the club is carved in southern Northwest Coast style with a large face, band eyebrows, raised flat triangular shaped nose, orbs and eyes outlined, mouth with the corners bent down and slightly protruding tongue. The finish of the face is simple and effective, probably executed with a curved knife. The back of the head has a number of iron nails hammered in, perhaps relating to some material such as cedar bark formerly attached to the club as hair. Or, since the club is damaged and split at this point, the nails may relate to native repairs. The body of the club, eyebrows, orbas and mouth are stained in a slightly darker brown than the rest of the face. The club is carved from a central section of a large trunk.
